name: BMX
//: **THE TWO SCOPES A HOST INJECTS INTO ARE PART OF BMX'S PROMISE, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL.**
BMX captures a block's head and a slot's expression OPAQUELY and hands them to the host — that
is BOUNDARY.md's whole rule. Highlighting has to say the same thing, or an editor would be
claiming to know what `on:click=save(line.id)` means when the format does not.
So the head and the expression get their own named scopes and NOTHING inside them is coloured
here:
meta.block.head.bmx           everything after a block's name
meta.slot.expression.bmx      the text between {{ and }}
meta.inline-block.head.bmx    the text between [ and ] of an inline block
A host injects with `injectionSelector: "L:meta.slot.expression.bmx"` and colours its own
expression language there. Two hosts can do it differently in the same editor and neither has to
patch this file. **These three names are therefore a compatibility surface**: renaming one
breaks every host's grammar, so it is a major change under VERSIONING.md, exactly like renaming
an AST field.
Order matters twice below. A fenced code block wins over everything, because §5 says its content
is never parsed — a `{{` inside one is text and colouring it as a slot would be a lie an author
could not turn off. And a longer ::: fence must be tried before a shorter one, or `::::` reads as
`:::` followed by a stray colon.

fenced-code.//: First, and its content has no patterns at all. §5: nothing inside is parsed.
fenced-code.name: markup.raw.block.bmx

block-4.//: A four-or-longer fence, tried before three so nesting reads correctly.
block-4.name: meta.block.bmx

//: The ONLY parts of a head BMX has an opinion about, per §4a: `.class` and `#id`. Everything
else stays bare inside `meta.block.head.bmx` for a host to claim — including `title="x"` and
`on:click=save(n)`, which look like attributes and are not the format's business.

escape.//: §3: only these five may be escaped, so only these are coloured as an escape.
escape.name: constant.character.escape.bmx

code-span.//: Before slots: a `{{ x }}` inside backticks is text, and colouring it would be a lie.
code-span.name: markup.inline.raw.bmx

//: **The injection point.** The expression is not coloured here, on purpose: BMX does not know
what a host's expression language is. A host injects into
`meta.slot.expression.bmx` and gets its own colours with no change to this file.
slot.name: meta.slot.bmx

//: `::key[Ctrl+S]::`. Deliberately coloured differently from a slot, because the guarantee
differs: a slot's value is always escaped, an inline block is a call to something the host
declared. An author should be able to tell at a glance which one can produce markup.
